title: Wax-weld three blade patterns into a casting cluster with a hot knife, holding each square and still until the wax sets
instruction: Weld the three loose blue wax blade patterns onto the sprue at the three empty scribed marks. For each: hold it by the two ends of its platform with its gate end against the mark, pass the hot knife between the gate end and the sprue so both faces melt, take the knife out, press the gate onto the sprue square, and keep the pattern still until the wax sets before you let go. The knife touches only the gate end and the sprue, never any pattern's airfoil, platform or root, and nothing may knock the patterns already on the cluster. When all three are on, lay the knife back in its rest and move both hands clear.
context: Investment-cast parts, from turbine blades to implants, start as wax patterns welded by hand onto a wax tree; aero-engine blade clusters carry 6 to 30 patterns (Prasad, InTech 2012). Nearly all tree assembly is manual and it is the most labour-intensive step in the foundry; the wax room takes up to 30% of foundry labour, and the weld is made with a hot knife passed between the two wax surfaces (Puffer and Phipps, ACEEE 2003). Hand welds vary: patterns end up crooked or break off at the weld (US 6,889,743), and manual assembly is the main source of pattern distortion (US 5,350,002). Precision castings have been one of aerospace's biggest production bottlenecks since 2020 (BCG 2024). A pattern moved or let go while the wax sets falls off or is welded crooked, and each mark sits between patterns already on the cluster.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A steel assembly stand (120 x 120 x 8 mm) on an aluminium drip tray (160 x 160 x 2 mm), both fixed, centred at x 25, y 6. On it a blue-green wax pour cup (50 mm across, 25 mm tall, mouth down) and a blue-green wax sprue, 25 x 25 mm square and 150 mm tall, standing on the cup (fixed). Three pairs of scribed lines on the sprue's face toward the tray (-y) mark gate positions centred 7.5, 11.0 and 14.5 cm above the table. Already welded on the sprue by their gates: three blue wax blade patterns, one on the -y face at 4.0 cm, two on the +x face at 7.5 and 11.0 cm. Three loose blue injection-wax turbine-blade patterns, 17 g each, lie level in a grey foam tray (160 x 124 x 12 mm slab with a bar under the gates and one under the airfoils) at x 20, 25 and 30, gate end faces at y -17, gates pointing +y: each is a 12 x 12 x 45 mm gate, an 18 x 15 x 14 mm fir-tree root, a 30 x 4 x 22 mm platform and a twisted, cambered airfoil 50 mm long, 24 mm chord and 6 mm thick, 114 mm overall. An electric wax knife (black handpiece 12 mm across and 130 mm long; flat steel blade 25 x 12 x 0.8 mm on a 30 mm shank; 40 g) lies level in its rest, which has a blade guard, at x 33, y 26, blade toward +x; its cord leaves the handle's end and runs off the table's left edge to the temperature controller on a stand beside the table. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured at the end with a steel rule, an engineer's square and photos; the trial video for the at-any-time rules. Score 0 if at any time a pattern already on the cluster is knocked 2 mm or 2 degrees out of place (checked at the end against a printed locating template, and on the video), a loose pattern's 30 mm platform is squeezed 1 mm or more narrower between a gripper's fingers (caliper after the trial), or the hot blade touches a gripper's finger. Each loose pattern scores 0.25 if at the end it hangs from the sprue by its own weld with no finger within 1 cm of it, its gate centred within 3 mm of an empty mark (one pattern per mark) and square to the sprue's face within 3 degrees; minus 0.10 if its gate melted back (the blade held in the joint over 8 s: the gate 3 mm short by rule). Minus 0.10 for each pattern whose airfoil, platform or root the blade touched (a melt mark 1 mm or more across on the photo). Only once a pattern scores: 0.15 for the knife lying back in its rest, and 0.10 for every finger 3 cm or more from the knife, the patterns and the sprue, held 1 s. 1.0 needs all three welded sound, the knife in its rest and the hands clear, held 1 s. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0. Possible scores: 0 to 1.0 in steps of 0.05.
reset_notes: Patterns are poured in batches ahead of time in the RTV silicone mould made from the printable master in assets/ (about 10 minutes each, 17 g of blue injection wax); three per trial. Cut the three new welds off the sprue with the warm knife and scrape the face flat at the marks (about 2 minutes); replace the sprue when a mark's face has been scraped back 1 mm, about every 10 trials. The cluster's three welded patterns are reused: check them against the printed locating template and re-weld one that has moved. Let the knife cool in its rest before resetting.
fidelity: Rigid wax parts; each loose pattern hangs on six free joints, so it moves freely and falls if let go. Melting is a declared rule: heat counts only while the blade touches the gate end and the sprue at a mark at once, 2 to 8 s (past 8 s the gate melts back 3 mm); the gate must touch that mark within 4 s, may be set square in the first 2 s, then stay within 1 mm and 2 degrees for 10 s; its joints then lock. Times are estimates. No drips, fillet or cord.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (ran all 4,800 steps, no refusal; it never lifted a pattern); demo: 1.0 (scripted, 2,794 steps)
